title: One owned thing: Tämä on …
focus: Identify one owned thing with Tämä on and the already learned owner endings.

exercises.prompt: Write “This is their game.” in Finnish. Begin with Tämä on. Use peli (“game”).
exercises.explanation: Tämä on identifies one thing. The ending -nsä identifies their ownership.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Simple ownership identity sentences: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Tämä identifies one thing.
Use on with one thing, independently of how many people own it.
Heidän is the personal owner form of he; it selects -nsä.
peli (“game”) + -nsä = pelinsä. The same possessed form can name one or several things; this sentence names one.

Correct: Tämä on identifies one thing. The ending -nsä identifies their ownership.
Use Tämä on for one thing, and keep the owner’s possessive ending.

exercises.prompt: Write “This is your car.” in Finnish. Begin with Tämä on. Address a group. Use auto (“car”).
exercises.explanation: Tämä on identifies one thing. The ending -nne identifies your ownership.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Simple ownership identity sentences: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Tämä identifies one thing.
Use on with one thing, independently of how many people own it.
Teidän is the personal owner form of te; it selects -nne.
auto (“car”) + -nne = autonne. The same possessed form can name one or several things; this sentence names one.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Drop the noun’s plural -t before -nne: use autonne.
Keep the possessive ending -nne even when the owner pronoun is present or omitted.
Teidän needs -nne; changing the ending changes the owner.
